''See also: [[The mask Timeline]]''

== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|The mask is a unique, dual-colored artifact constructed from two different metals: one side consists of rough black [[Iron|iron]] and the other is polished, mirror-like [[Tartarus steel]]. These two halves are joined by a jagged, uneven seam rather than a smooth line. The object features narrow slits for eyes but lacks any opening for the mouth or visible means of attachment, such as straps; instead, it binds itself to the wearer's head through unknown means. Originally, the mask was part of a larger tool designed to enhance the abilities of [[Travelers]] by allowing them to access [[Valinhall]] more effectively, featuring built-in safety mechanisms to prevent users from exhausting their life force. However, the original was shattered in a past conflict. The current version is a reconstructed iteration made from those remnants and attuned to a specific [[Territory]]. While it grants the wearer immense power—potentially rivaling that of an [[Incarnation]] by allowing a deeper connection to [[Valinhall]]—it lacks the original's safety restraints. Using the mask carries significant risks, including the possibility of being sensed and summoned by an [[Incarnation]], which could lead to the wearer's death.}}

== The Crimson Vault ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|Constructed from both polished-[[steel]] silver and wrought-[[Iron|iron]] black, this mask features a dual-sided appearance. [[Simon]] suspects the artifact originates from [[Ragnarus the Crimson Vault|Ragnarus]]. The object possesses the ability to bind a user with patterns resembling [[black chains]], though it cannot function outside of the [[Territory]] without being attuned. To achieve attunement, the mask must be bound to a specific challenge within a particular room.}}

== City of Light ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|Constructed of half black [[Iron|iron]] and half mirrored [[steel]] with two narrow eye slits, the mask was originally designed to strengthen other [[Travelers]] through built-in safety measures meant to prevent them from burning away their lives. The artifact allows a user to draw more deeply on [[Valinhall]] and provides the ability to utilize essence and [[steel]] without exhaustion, though it causes [[chains]] to grow upon the wearer. While [[Simon]] eventually pulls out and puts on the mask to call upon his powers with impunity, another version exists belonging to [[Kai]], which features a white and gray design with rectangular eye slits and no mouth.}}
